johanna catharina mountjoy of indwe — – jun 1911, indwe · mountjoy she joined the dutch reformed congregation at indwe on 23 july 1907, arriving from barkly oost — six weeks after willem hermanus booijzen was confirmed in the same church — and the register’s last column records her dead there in june 1911. a mountjoy and a booyzen in one small colliery congregation, twenty-two years after the two families stood at the same font at barkly oost.

william henry keys 1854 – — · mountjoy married johanna catharina mountjoy, baptised at burgersdorp on 29 february 1860 — a daughter of george mountjoy and maria sophia botha, which this archive had been asking about and can now answer. eight children baptised across dordrecht, barkly east and barkly west between 1878 and 1898: robert byron, william henry, james jonathan, george, lancelott byron, cecil frederik, rachel anna maria and herklaas edward johannes. the mountjoy forenames crossing into a third surname, exactly as the barry names crossed into the daschners — and byron twice, which appears nowhere else in this archive.

mary elizabeth kolbe — – bef. 1867 · kolbe margaretha's sister, and the woman who married george frederick enslin — which is the whole answer to a contradiction this archive carried as serious, that margaretha appeared to marry enslin while married to john barry. it was resolved from margaret downing's 1867 death notice. the burgersdorp register of 23 october 1853 shows it instead: the two sisters baptising a son each, two entries apart, on one page.

q: william barry 23 aug 1853, baptised 23 oct 1853 at burgersdorp – — · barry found twice in one day. he came in on the 1915 death notice of his mother margaretha kolbe, estate 1291, which names nine children where his father's names eight — and then the burgersdorp doopregister produced his baptism: william fredrik, born 23 august 1853, christened 23 october, godparents john kolbe, anna van der merwe and george kolbe. two of the three are his mother's brothers. a second william frederick thomas was baptised in 1861 and this archive cannot say whether the first died or a clerk erred — a doubt re-surfaced, and briefly mistaken for a new find, when the index was asked for every barry child of a kolbe mother. he is not on his father's notice, not on the cape rebel roll, and nowhere else in this archive. his father's 1903 registration said eleven children; with william there are nine named and two still missing.
kathleen mary barry — – — · barry named on the 1915 death notice.

john augustus barry ii 13 mar 1847, baptised 12 apr 1847 – — · barry the eldest son on the 1915 notice, carrying his father's name exactly — which is why this archive calls the father john augustus barry i. his own documents call him simply john barry, and that is the third man in this family the name has to be shared out between. his birth date does one more job than it looks: being hard, off a register, it is what forces his brother james henry's “about 1847” to move.

margaret mary bedford — – — · barry born barry, and on the 1915 notice as married to tom bedford. the tree carries a margaretha louisa maria who married thomas bedford in 1875; the notice gives her as margaret mary, and the archive has not reconciled the two.

johan gottlieb kolbe 1765 – 1845 · kolbe tailor. died at 34 conduit street, mayfair — not lamb's conduit street; the tree's photograph is of the wrong building. buried at the german savoy church, strand.

george augustus kolbe 1802 – 1 dec 1844, “wurtemburg”, colesberg · kolbe 1820 settler — the nautilus, owen's party, algoa bay 14 apr 1820. married at sixteen on a sworn falsehood. preached across the orange river. his grandson could not name him in 1915.

tersia booyzen living – — · testimony recorded the name-change and anglo-boer war account on the myheritage tree, as told to her by her father.

graaff-reinet town, cape colony · karoo where this family is oldest. johanna catharina montjoy was born here on 30 april 1819 and james montjoy married anna catharina slier here on 9 march 1817. the dutch reformed baptism registers here carry the family from 1788 to 1857.

cradock town, cape colony · karoo a saddler's town, and the top of the mountjoy line. james montjoy died here in september 1827 owning a house and erf worth £90; his son george learned his trade here and married here in 1848.

achter sneeuwberg farming district · karoo “behind the sneeuberg.” the place column of the 1851 baptism register, which tells us the family was farming out beyond the mountain rather than living in cradock town.

s: Farm · Brak River, later Middelburg district
q: zevenfontein farm · brak river, later middelburg district the family farm across two death notices twenty-one years apart — and the district boundary moved under it. johanna catharina died here in 1863 when it was reckoned brak river, port elizabeth; her husband died here in 1884 when it was middelburg.

barkly east town and district · north-eastern cape the district the family belongs to for two generations, and the most rebellious corner of the colony in 1899–1902. its doop register holds the booyzen and mountjoy baptisms on facing pages. it is also the only place in this archive where an estate is itemised: a retired builder's savings-bank deposit, a house on lot 380 let at fifty shillings a month, and a village's worth of unpaid accounts — two butchers, a doctor and a burial society.

manorowen farm · barkly east the barry farm, and now documented as john barry's own house rather than only his son's. the 1903 registration of his death gives his residence and his place of death as manor owen, ward iv, with his son richard barry living at the same address and signing as “son present at death”. margaretha kolbe died here in 1915. harriet louisa barry, eighteen, lived here and was buried here in 1912. three deaths in this family on one farm in twelve years.

jerpoint farm · cape colony named for an abbey in county kilkenny — the first irish place name this archive has found anywhere near the barrys, whose irish origin it has never been able to place. a richard peter barry, plaasboer of jerpoint, is on the cape rebel roll.
ivanhoe farm · barkly east / wodehouse fred j. barry farmed here and was tried as a cape rebel in june 1901 — the same district and the same month as schoeman of caerlaverock.

caerlaverock farm · wodehouse / barkly east named for a castle in dumfriesshire. the family married in this house in july 1901 — five weeks after its owner, daniel willem schoeman, was tried as a cape rebel. he signed the register.

dordrecht town · wodehouse where this side of the family married, and where its in-laws lived. hercules johannes mountjoy married maria sophia van niekerk here on 8 october 1888, aged 22 — a year before the 1889 font at barkly oost. james john mountjoy and maria louisa bertha kumm gave dordrecht as their place of last marriage too, on two death notices filed at barkly east fifty years later. and it is where maria sophia’s mother died, at her own house, in december 1902.

indwe colliery town · north-eastern cape a colliery town, and this archive took three passes to notice that the word matters. willem hermanus booyzen died at doorn street, indwe, on 13 september 1905 of an ulcer of the stomach. his daughter catharina maria sophia married joseph heinrich daschner here. and his son — a son this archive did not know it had — was confirmed here in 1907 at twenty-one, married here in 1908 as a mijnwerker of dugmore mijn, and had two children baptised here in 1908 and 1910, both entered onecht. their grandmother kathleen barry stood godmother at the first font, three years after she was widowed in this town. indwe is where the family testimony's last line turns out to be true, in the wrong province.

lady grey town · north-eastern cape he is entered as a boer — farmer — of lady grey at his marriage in 1879, and a mason at his death in 1905. something took the land away in between, and the 1884 estate says it may already have been gone.
wodehouse district · north-eastern cape hercules johannes mountjoy died here on 12 may 1941, aged 74 — and the cape town archives hold no estate file for him under any spelling.

colesberg town · northern cape midlands george augustus kolbe, the 1820 settler, died on the farm “wurtemburg” in this district on 1 december 1844. his widow signed the death notice here in january 1845, and the 1840 montjoy notice was signed here too.

burgersdorp town · north-eastern cape george augustus kolbe and margaret downing lie under a cut-stone monument in the old cemetery here — names, london birthplaces, farm and dates carved on it, about forty miles from where their grandson wrote that he could not name them.
johannesburg city · witwatersrand where the family arrives with nothing and where the archive's starting point was born. forest hill, mayfair, fordsburg and germiston all appear on its certificates.
west park cemetery cemetery · johannesburg anna pretorius was buried here in 1944 and her husband three years later, three days after he died.
brixton cemetery cemetery · johannesburg kathleen barry's intended place of burial on her 1940 death form — a mile and a half from the mayfair house, and a long way from barkly east.
vereeniging town · transvaal where george downing mountjoy booyzen married anna johanna maria pretorius on 30 december 1924 — she aged eighteen, with her father's written consent.

rustenburg town · transvaal where the male line's oldest documented man died. petrus jacobus booysen, born at graaff-reinet about 1788, died in this district on 1 september 1876, eighty-eight years old, a widower, with nothing to leave — "niets nagelaten. niets bekend." his sterfkennis was written at the farm brakfontein on 14 september and signed by his son hendrik stefanus. it is the single most important place on this map, because it destroys the idea that this family reached the transvaal by railway in the twentieth century.
soho, london parish · middlesex st anne's, soho, where george augustus kolbe was baptised on 2 february 1803, son of john gottlob and mary. the register notes 410 baptisms for the year 1802.

shoreditch parish · london st leonard's, where george augustus kolbe married margaret downing in 1819 on a sworn falsehood — both swore they were twenty-one; he was sixteen and she fifteen. she signed with a mark.

conduit street street · mayfair, london 34 conduit street, where johan gottlieb kolbe the tailor died in 1845 — not lamb's conduit street, which is where the family tree put him and where its photograph shows the wrong building.

german savoy church church · strand, london where johan gottlieb kolbe was actually buried on 26 november 1845, entry 55, grave 7 — not st john the baptist, leamington, warwickshire, as the tree has it. the correction makes the family more coherent, not less: they are german lutherans of the savoy.

heilbron town · orange free state where the only booysen in the whole joiners register comes from — j. j. booysen, four hundred miles from barkly east and in a different country at the time. it matters because the family's account of the name change rests on there having been booysen joiners.

middelburg town and district · cape colony zevenfontein fell in this district by 1884. and a p. j. booyzen — spelled with the z — was a police constable at the middelburg police office in 1904, 1905 and 1907, with mortgage bonds in 1904 and 1906. not shown to be a relative.

stutterheim town · eastern cape ferdinand kumm died here on 20 october 1903 — and his death notice is the document an external source mistook for james jonathan mountjoy's. the town returned to this archive from a different direction entirely: joseph heinrich daschner, who married a booyzen daughter at indwe, was born here about november 1883.

brisbane city · queensland, australia where the line reaches now. the sixteen booyzens recorded in australia are likely a separate migration; this family arrived through the lerena and defranceski marriages rather than under the booyzen name.

pretoria city · transvaal where the transvaal master of the supreme court sat, and so where this family's later estates were filed — the depot this archive spent its whole life not searching. stephanus francois booyzen died at east lynne, on its eastern edge, in 1940.

marico district · western transvaal a substantial booyzen farming district — and this archive can no longer say whose. seven booyzen claims for compensation as burghers were filed here in 1903–04, and the booyzen children who died in the johannesburg and vereeniging camps came from farms in this district. this entry used to call them "emphatically someone else's". that judgement rested on the belief that this family was in the cape until about 1907 — and the 1876 sterfkennis at rustenburg, one district east, shows it was not. no document links this family to any of the seven claims. no document rules it out either. unresolved is the honest word. 13 september 2026: and now a documented booysen marriage in the district. hendrik stephanus booysen — seventh child on the 1876 sterfkennis, son of the direct ancestor — married charlotta elizabetha dormehl at zeerust, the principal town of marico. it still links this family to none of the seven compensation claims. it does mean the last of the three districts has had one of these people standing in it, and the sentence this archive withdrew was wronger than it knew.
mossel bay town · southern cape where stephanus francois booyzen married beatrix magdalena catharina boshoff — six hundred miles from where he was born and eight hundred from where he died.
potchefstroom town · transvaal a booyzen presence from at least 1860, when jan booyzen paid his marriage fee to the government here. whether the line connects to this family is unproven.

booysens suburb, johannesburg · witwatersrand not a family place — a trap. booysens is a mining suburb south of the johannesburg city centre, a couple of miles from forest hill and kenilworth where this family actually lived in the 1940s. it means every name-index search for booysen in johannesburg returns people whose only connection to the word is an address. the archive met it head-on: a death notice indexed under the surname daschner turned out to belong to charles bruce rennie, a miner of booysens, and nothing else about him touches this family at all.

brakfontein farm · district rustenburg, transvaal the farm where the oldest document in this archive was written. on 14 september 1876, thirteen days after the death, somebody at brakfontein filled in sterfkennis no. 678 for petrus jacobus booijsen, aged 88, and wrote the names of his parents on line 3. fifteen years later it takes two more: his son's wife on 9 may 1891 and their son five days after her. and in 1892 hendrik stefanus, marrying again at zeerust, still gives brakfontein as his home — sixteen years on the same ground. the coordinates are approximate: the district is certain, the farm is not yet placed.

lichtenburg district · western transvaal where this family's western transvaal branch is, and it is a branch rather than a lead now. jan gerthardus lodewikus booijsen — fifth of the eight children on the 1876 sterfkennis, born district graaff-reinet about 1818 — died on the farm vaalbank in this district on 25 may 1885, estate tab mhg o/2899. his daughter magdalena susanna maria died on the same farm on 1 may 1920, and her sterfkennis names him. lichtenburg is one district west of rustenburg, where his father died in 1876, and one district east of marico.

dugmore mine colliery · indwe, district wodehouse where a booyzen worked underground. the indwe marriage register of 21 september 1908 gives both bride and groom's dwelling place as “dugmore mijn” and the groom's trade as “mijnwerker”. it is the only mine anywhere in this archive attached to a named member of this family, and it is coal in the cape rather than gold on the rand. the coordinates are approximate — the workings were at indwe and the exact site is not yet fixed.

vaalbank farm · district lichtenburg, transvaal one farm, two deaths, thirty-five years apart, and the same family on it both times. jan gerthardus lodewikus booijsen — born district graaff-reinet about 1818, fifth child on the 1876 sterfkennis — died here on 25 may 1885. his daughter magdalena susanna maria, born about 1860, died here on 1 may 1920. it is the clearest evidence this archive has that the family did not merely pass through the western transvaal but settled in it, two generations before anyone reached johannesburg. the coordinates are approximate: the district is certain, the farm is not yet placed.

cherryville farm · district barkly east the third named barry farm, after manorowen and jerpoint. harriet louisa barry, eighteen, died here of typhoid on 7 september 1912 after thirty days' illness and was carried back to manorowen to be buried. her father, who signed the form, gave his own residence as manorowen — so cherryville is somewhere the family worked rather than lived, or another barry household entirely. the coordinates are approximate.

slang river locality · north-eastern cape where dorothea regina barry, daughter of hendrik nicholaas barry and anna johanna maria schoeman, was baptised on 3 april 1892. from the index rather than the register, and placed only approximately.

koedoesfontein farm · district rustenburg, transvaal where hendrik stephanus booysen died on 11 may 1908, aged seventy-nine, in the house of his son-in-law willem grobelaar. a farmer with no movable property, some land, and mutual wills with both of his dead wives. thirty-two years earlier he had signed his own father's sterfkennis at brakfontein, one district over. the coordinates are approximate.

zeerust town, district marico · transvaal the principal town of marico, and the district this archive spent weeks holding at arm's length with the sentence “they are not this family, who were cape”. hendrik stefanus booijzen married here on 14 april 1892 — 63, a widower of brakfontein — and signed his second wife's death notice here in august 1902. the sentence is withdrawn.

q: driefontein farm, groot marico · district marico, transvaal charlotta elizabeth dormehl's own place. she gave it as her home when she married at zeerust in april 1892, and she died there on 6 february 1902 — three months before the peace, and ten years into a marriage to a man who farmed a hundred miles away at brakfontein. she never moved to him. the coordinates are approximate: the district is certain, the farm is not placed.

zwartruggens town · transvaal where diederik arnoldus booysen was born about august 1887 and lived as a karweier — a transport rider. his 1935 sterfkennis is the first document in this archive printed in afrikaans rather than dutch or english, and it names his parents: ockert johannes stephanus booysen and elizabeth johanna sophia myburgh, both by then dead.

voorbedacht no. 401 farm · district rustenburg, transvaal where diederik arnoldus booysen died on 1 march 1935, aged 47 years 7 months, with an estate over £300 and a will — the largest booysen estate this archive has read. a numbered farm, which is how the transvaal registered land. coordinates approximate.

klerksdorp town · transvaal where ockert johannes stephanus booysen died on 16 january 1921, aged 69 — the man who signed his father's death notice in 1908 and who carried his mother's father's name out of the district of cradock and into the western transvaal. it is a civil registration and it names no parents, which is why this archive keeps going back to sterfkennisse. he has no estate file of his own.

market street, pretoria street · pretoria, transvaal elizabetha margaretha booijzen, born marais, died in a zinc building in market street on 1 june 1900 — the capital's main street, four days before lord roberts entered the town. her husband david schalk booijzen, the direct ancestor's brother, did not file her death notice for three years and nine months, and against the question about movable property he wrote “none. compensation claim filed.”

turffontein suburb · johannesburg, transvaal 18 anderson street. richard peter booyzen, twenty-four, married, a sawyer, died here of influenza and pneumonia on 25 october 1918 after eleven days — the centre of black october, which killed some fourteen thousand people on the rand in six weeks. he was buried at brixton two days later. his birthplace on the form is the cape of good hope: born in the north-eastern cape, dead in a johannesburg mining suburb at twenty-four.

mayfair suburb · johannesburg, transvaal this archive has had mayfair as a word on two pages and never as an address. kathleen barry died here in 1940. her great-granddaughter catherine mary sophia booyzen was married at st joseph's, mayfair on 15 january 1949 — the hinge into the lerena archive. and her son henry james booyzen was living at 3 15th avenue when he died in 1956. three generations in one suburb, and the cemetery register is what finally gave it a street number.

roodepoort town · west rand, transvaal hendrik stephanus nicolaas booysen — baptised at rustenburg in 1882, dead at kempton park in 1959 — was buried in the central cemetery of the municipality of roodepoort–maraisburg on 12 october 1959, section i d.r., entry 96. this archive published him as buried at johannesburg for an afternoon because the familysearch collection carries that title for every register inside it.

goedehoop place · pretoria, transvaal two men of this story lived here. charles petrus barend lowies, a hawker born in the district of cradock about october 1848, is “of goedehoop, pretoria” on his 1905 death notice — he died in the pretoria lunatic asylum on 5 june that year, leaving twelve children, six still minors. and david schalk booijzen, born in the district of cradock in june 1848, gives goede hoop, pretoria as his home on the register when he marries lowies's widow on 27 november, five months and twenty-two days later. this archive read that register first and wrote the address down without knowing what it meant. coordinates approximate.
